summary: `gone` includes every rename's old name even when a new file now exists at that path. buildGraph then drops that live file from the graph, and selectLanes (line 200) marks it `removed (no lane owed) — old name of <new>`. A new source file there skips the PREGATE_NO_LANE check, and a new test there never runs.
evidence: Scratch repro (<sandbox>/repro.test.ts, using test/helpers/pregate-fixture). Committed `git mv lib/util.js lib/util2.js`, then wrote a new untracked lib/util.js. Branch: no PREGATE_NO_LANE, lines include `removed (no lane owed): lib/util.js — old name of lib/util2.js`. Same script on main: `"code": "PREGATE_NO_LANE"`, `FAIL lanes — lib/util.js has no test lane`. Renaming test/util.test.js and re-creating a failing test/util.test.js: branch `ran: node --test 'test/util2.test.js'` (new test skipped), main `ran: node --test 'test/util.test.js' 'test/util2.test.js'`. Code: `const gone = touched.flatMap(t => [t.status === 'D' ? t.path : null, t.renamedFrom ?? null])` and in import-graph.ts `listRepoFiles(repoRoot).filter(f => !gone.has(f))`; context.ts:126-130 lets a touched entry with status 'A' share its path with another entry's renamedFrom.

summary: Any deleted non-test file that no test reaches is waived as 'no lane owed — no remaining test references it', even when remaining untested product code still imports it. A deletion that leaves a broken import now passes `lanes`, where main failed with PREGATE_NO_LANE.
evidence: Fixture: base adds lib/a.js and lib/b.js (`require('./a.js')`, no tests); branch deletes lib/a.js. Branch: lanes status=pass, line 'removed (no lane owed): lib/a.js — no remaining test references it'. Same probe on a main worktree: status=fail, code=PREGATE_NO_LANE, 'FAIL lanes — lib/a.js has no test lane'. removedPath: `if (!isTestFile(file)) return { removed: { file, note: 'no remaining test references it', lostCoverage: [] }, suite: [] };` never checks graph.reverse for importers still in the tree.

summary: The deleted-test handling (owning suite, lost-coverage report) applies only to files isTestFile matches, so a deleted Rust integration test (crate tests/*.rs, which rust.ts finds separately) is treated as a plain deleted file. It is waived without naming the crate that lost its last test, contrary to the new docs/pregate.md contract.
evidence: Fixture: crate gamma with src/lib.rs (no #[cfg(test)]) and tests/g.rs; branch deletes engine/crates/gamma/tests/g.rs. Lanes output: status=pass, detail 'nothing touched selects a test; 1 removed path(s)', line 'removed (no lane owed): engine/crates/gamma/tests/g.rs — no remaining test references it' (no 'coverage removed'). The equivalent Python probe correctly prints 'coverage removed: pkg/__init__.py pkg/mod.py have no remaining test'. goneSources (lane-selection.ts:139) and removedPath (line 116) both gate on isTestFile, whose TEST_FILE_RE has no Rust form.
